description: Recorded measurements that back an evidence claim. A capability value cites one as 'measurement:<id>' in its evidence mapping, the same way it cites 'make:<target>' or 'example:<case>'. The difference is what the source is: a make target or example is re-runnable on demand, while a measurement is a run that already happened and cannot be cheaply repeated - a cluster campaign, a refinement study, a reference comparison. Recording it here is what lets a later reader, human or agent, see that the question was already answered, on what, and to what threshold, instead of running it again.

record_contract.id: stable identifier, referenced as measurement:<id> and cited by name in the capability entry
record_contract.question: the single question the campaign was run to answer
record_contract.date: ISO date the measurement was taken
record_contract.commit: repository revision the measurement was taken at
record_contract.environment: machine, scheduler, and rank layout the run actually used
record_contract.configuration: case, grid, and the settings that determine the result
record_contract.result: what was measured, the threshold it was judged against, and the verdict: met, not-met, or inconclusive
record_contract.limitations: what this measurement does not establish; required, and 'none' is not an acceptable value
record_contract.artifacts: committed derived data supporting the result; may be empty when the numbers in 'result' are the whole record

records.question: Does the matrix-free Newton-Krylov momentum path with the frozen_momentum_jacobian point-block preconditioner run production-size curved-duct cases to completion, with every physical step converged and committed and the pressure projection divergence-free, across a three-grid refinement study?

records.configuration: Laminar flow through the Humphrey, Taylor & Whitelaw (1977) square-duct 90-degree bend: grid.gen sweep, unit square cross-section, path straight 5 D, arc radius 2.3 D through 90 degrees, straight 7 D; uniform spacing. Three grids, refined uniformly in all three directions: 32 x 32 x 256, 48 x 48 x 384 and 64 x 64 x 512 cells. Re = 790 (density 1, viscosity 1/790, unit length and velocity). Inlet prescribed_flow with a generated square_duct_poiseuille profile (bulk 1); noslip walls; conservation outlet; streamwise_constant initial condition; no LES, wall function, IBM or particles. Momentum: Newton Krylov, central convection, finite_difference/matrix_free Jacobian, preconditioner frozen_momentum_jacobian with point_block structure, SNES newtonls with backtracking, snes rtol 1e-8 (32-cell grid) or 1e-6 (48 and 64), GMRES ksp rtol 1e-6, max_it 400, restart 80, Eisenstat-Walker adaptive linear tolerance on. Pressure: FGMRES with four-level multiplicative multigrid, coarse level preonly + redundant. dt = 0.02, 0.0133 and 0.01 (streamwise CFL held below 1), 3000, 4500 and 6000 steps, physical time 60 on each grid. Near-wall diffusion number nu*dt/dx^2 is about 0.03 to 0.05.

result.measured: All 13,500 physical steps (3000 + 4500 + 6000) appear in Momentum_Solver_Newton_Krylov_Summary_Block_0.log with no missing or duplicate steps, every one with state committed and the frozen_momentum_jacobian / point_block preconditioner. Termination reasons: CONVERGED_SNORM_RELATIVE 2993 / 3185 / 4426 and CONVERGED_FNORM_RELATIVE 7 / 1315 / 1574 on the 32 / 48 / 64 grids. Newton iterations per step 2 to 5; Krylov iterations per step at most 25 / 19 / 18, median 4, falling from 14-25 at start-up to 3-4 at steady state; largest final nonlinear norm 8.2e-9 / 1.5e-6 / 4.0e-6. Continuity_Metrics.log: maximum divergence over every step 4.60e-10 / 3.37e-10 / 3.13e-10, maximum net boundary flux 1.6e-15 / 2.0e-15 / 8.9e-15. All three runs reached steady state (solution_convergence u_abs_l2 3.6e-9 / 4.5e-9 / 4.9e-9 at the final step) and the solver output reached 100 percent. Exploratory accuracy context, not part of the verdict: against Humphrey, Taylor & Whitelaw (1977) Fig. 2, digitised (299 of 300 points), the streamwise-velocity RMS difference at 0 / 30 / 60 / 90 degrees is 0.074 / 0.182 / 0.177 / 0.135 U_b on the 64 grid; the 48-to-64 change is 0.001-0.013 U_b RMS; a Celik et al. (2008) three-grid analysis on the symmetry plane gives apparent order 1.9-2.7 and absolute GCI_fine at most 0.03 U_b; the experiment's own X_H = -5 profile differs from the exact fully developed solution by 0.078 RMS.
result.threshold: Retrospective production-execution criterion, the same as the one applied to preconditioner none in turbulent-channel-nk-2026-09-29: every inspected physical step converges and commits, pressure-projected divergence stays below 1e-9, and each run completes. Applied during review, not preregistered. Agreement with the experiment is a separate question and is not part of this verdict.

records.limitations: Laminar, steady, low-Re flow in one geometry: the mass term dominates the operator (near-wall diffusion number about 0.03-0.05), which is the regime a same-cell point block is expected to handle. No run with preconditioner none on these cases, so no Krylov-count or wall-time benefit is established and no performance claim is made. The current point block is untested at high Reynolds number on wall-resolved grids: the only such run (Re 40,000, 193 x 193 x 513, diffusion number about 1.1, dt 0.01) collapsed with DIVERGED_LINEAR_SOLVE at step 233, but it was built from 4aafb04, before the transpose fix d4f5944, so it says nothing about the present implementation in either direction. Turbulence models, wall functions, periodic and driven boundaries, IBM and multiblock are not exercised. One rank count and layout; no restart, no scaling study. The wall-face eddy viscosity (issue #8) is irrelevant at stencil width zero and is not tested. The accuracy figures depend on digitised reference data and on station planes placed at the nearest grid k-index (up to 0.76 degrees apart across grids).

records.question: Does the dual-time Picard momentum solver with the multigrid pressure projection reproduce laminar square-duct Poiseuille flow, and at what spatial order?
records.commit: d6fff0f plus the uncommitted 2026-09-18 registry-reset working tree (validation refusals, legacy-flag removal, documentation); no momentum, pressure, particle, or metric numerics differ from d6fff0f
records.environment: Local WSL2 workstation, 12 cores, 7 GB RAM; PETSc 3.20.3 debug build (-O0 -g3) with MPICH; local mpiexec, no scheduler; 2, 4 and 6 ranks for n = 8, 16 and 24
records.configuration: Square duct, unit side, length 2, uniform grid_gen box of n x n x 2n cells for n = 8, 16, 24. Re = 10 (density 10, viscosity 1, U = L = 1). -Zeta INLET prescribed_flow with a generated square_duct_poiseuille source (bulk velocity 1, 101 terms), four noslip WALL faces, +Zeta OUTLET conservation. Constant plug initial field. dt = 0.05 for 120 steps (t = 6, about twelve slowest viscous time constants). Dual Time Picard Jameson RK with the flat_channel template controls (max 50 pseudo steps, residual relative tolerance 1e-3). Poisson fgmres + PCMG, 3 levels (2 for n = 8, see limitations).

result.measured: Streamwise velocity on the mid-length cell plane against the 201-term series at cell centres: relative L2 error 3.49e-2, 9.67e-3, 4.39e-3 (observed order 1.85 then 1.95); relative max error 4.00e-2, 1.09e-2, 4.93e-3. Axial pressure gradient over the middle half against -28.4536/Re: relative error 5.89e-2, 1.54e-2, 6.92e-3 (order 1.93 then 1.98). Inflow equals outflow to 1e-9; maximum divergence at most 5.5e-8; every physical step met its pseudo-time tolerance except one early transient step at n = 24; the steady field changed by less than 2e-10 per step at the end.
result.threshold: Errors decrease monotonically under refinement with observed order at least 1.8 in velocity and pressure gradient.

records.limitations: Steady laminar flow only: temporal order was not measured, and in fully developed duct flow the convective term vanishes, so convection is exercised only by the transient. Uniform Cartesian grid, so the curvilinear metric terms are identity-like; single block; Re = 10. The same duct at Re = 100 with dt = 1.0 hit the 50-iteration pseudo-time cap on every step and finished with an 18% pressure-gradient error, so the result holds only when steps converge. With 3 multigrid levels on the 9-node n = 8 grid the Poisson solve produced NaN; 2 levels were used there.

records.configuration: Re-characterization: the shipped examples/periodic_test/driven_channel/laminar case (Re = 100, 17 x 33 x 17 cells, initial_flux, dt = 0.05) for 10 steps. result.measured: Every Re = 100 step met its pseudo-time tolerance in 9 to 29 iterations (cap 50); the 2026-08-24 stall did not reproduce. At Re = 10 the maximum profile error relative to U_b was 1.81e-2, 5.15e-3, 1.37e-3 (observed order 1.98, 2.00 at the true spacing ratios); the applied force 2.7 x correction / dt matched 3 nu U_b / h^2 to 2.4%, 0.69%, 0.18%; the realized bulk velocity 0.90217, 0.90062, 0.90017 converged to the controller law U_target / (1 + 3 nu dt / (2.7 h^2)) = 0.9. records.environment: Local WSL2 workstation, 12 cores, 7 GB RAM; PETSc 3.20.3 debug build (-O0 -g3) with MPICH; local mpiexec, no scheduler; 1 rank per duct run, 2 ranks per bent-channel run
records.configuration: flat_channel duct, programmatic_c 17 x 17 x 33 cells, constant_velocity inlet, conservation outlet, 10 steps with momentum residual tolerance 1e-9 and Poisson relative tolerance 1e-12. Baseline: fgmres, 3 levels, 2 pre and 2 post sweeps, k semi-coarsening, coarse preonly + redundant LU, richardson + bjacobi smoothers. Each variant changed one setting; fields at step 10 were compared with the baseline and the maximum divergence read from Continuity_Metrics.log. cg was also compared with fgmres on the curved bent_channel grid (20 x 20 x 144, 5 steps). The fatal path and the multigrid projection carry unit tests in unit-poisson-rhs.

result.measured: Levels 1 and 2, full coarsening, pre/post sweeps 1/3, chebyshev + jacobi smoothers (169 iterations per step), a Krylov coarse solve (gmres + bjacobi, with its warning), level_1 max_it 4, and cg all reproduced the baseline velocity to at most 7e-15 and gauge-free pressure to at most 8e-14, with divergence at most 5.3e-13. On the curved grid cg matched fgmres to 4.9e-15 and 4.9e-14 with the true residual at 1e-12 or below every step. gmres, lgmres and bcgs failed with left and with right preconditioning: the Krylov residual fell to 1e-12 while the true residual stalled near 1e-3, leaving divergence of 1e-4 to 2.4e-4 and a pressure 3e-5 to 9e-5 off; they are now refused. Two options had no effect: per-level max_it, rtol and atol were emitted without PETSc's ksp_ prefix and left unused (now mapped), and poisson_solver.tolerance fed a field nothing read (now refused).
result.threshold: Each accepted option reproduces the baseline to 1e-10 with divergence below 1e-10; each emitted option is consumed by PETSc.

records.limitations: One duct and one curved grid at small size; the cost of each option was not characterized, and why non-flexible Krylov methods lose the true residual under this preconditioner was not diagnosed beyond the preconditioner not being a fixed linear operator.

records.environment: Local WSL2 workstation, ext4 working tree, 12 cores, 7 GB RAM; PETSc 3.20.3 debug build with MPICH; rclone 1.63.1 with a local-path remote; 1 rank
records.configuration: A fresh flat_channel workspace. A 43,208-byte PETSc Ucat field imported as initial-condition in each of copy, reflink, hardlink and reference mode, then used as a file initial condition in `picurv precompute --only initial-condition` twice per import. One byte of the shared source then changed and the hardlink and reference imports were precomputed again. All-or-nothing: one invocation with a grid_gen box grid (valid) and an ic_gen expression calling an undocumented function. A two-step solve with the grid_gen grid and a valid ic_gen field. `picurv storage prune --assets --unused-locally --dry-run` against a local-path rclone remote with no workspace archive.

result.measured: copy, hardlink and reference registered with the source checksum; hardlink shared the source inode. reflink failed with cp's 'Operation not supported', leaving no temporary file and no catalog record. After the source changed, the hardlink and reference imports each built a new object; the reference was used without a warning, since its registration checksum is recorded but not compared. The grid-plus-broken-IC invocation exited 1 on the ic.gen error, published nothing, and removed its temporary build directory. The solve completed and its manifest pinned the grid and initial-condition objects it used. Prune reported every object blocked - none had a verified remote copy - and removed nothing.

records.limitations: Local ext4 only: a successful reflink import, cluster filesystems where reflink and hardlink availability differ, and object accumulation at campaign scale were not exercised. Prune was exercised only to its blocked decision, because removal requires a verified remote workspace archive, which is storage.management's remote-scale question.

records.question: Does the IEM particle update make within-cell scalar variance decay at the model rate 2 Omega, Omega = C_IEM Gamma / V^(2/3), and does the solver's whole decay curve, including cell-to-cell exchange, match an independent implementation of the same discrete step?
records.commit: 3d9b7c1 plus the uncommitted 2026-10-01 working tree (registry and documentation only; no source under src/ or include/ differs from 3d9b7c1); simulator built 2026-10-01 after the last source change
records.environment: Local WSL2 workstation, 12 cores; PETSc 3.20.3 debug build (-O0 -g3) with MPICH; local mpiexec, no scheduler; 2 ranks
records.configuration: examples/brownian_motion adapted: unit cube, 8^3 uniform cells, WALL on every face, ZERO_FLOW analytical carrier, LES off, Gamma = nu/Sc = 1e-3; 32,768 Volume-seeded particles with models.physics.particles.fields Psi = where(uniform() < 0.5, 0, 1). Three runs: C_IEM = 2 (default) with dt = 0.01 for 1000 steps; C_IEM = 20 with dt = 0.01 for 200 steps; C_IEM = 200 with dt = 0.001 for 300 steps; checkpoints every 10 steps. Metric: pooled within-cell variance of Psi from each checkpoint's Psi and CellID, as a ratio to its t = 0 value. Reference: a NumPy emulation of the solver's step order (src/runloop.c: Brownian move, locate, remove particles outside the cube, relax toward the host cell's previous-step scattered mean, scatter), 8 seeds per configuration. Restart: the C_IEM = 20 run continued from its step-100 checkpoint with restart_mode load (picurv run --restart-from) to step 200. Cause of the late-time departure: the C_IEM = 20 run repeated with 131,072 particles (256 per cell, 4 ranks), and emulation variants with frozen particles, with the mean scattered after the move, and with 256 and 1024 particles per cell.

result.measured: Against the emulation, at every output step of all three runs: |z| <= 2.06 (z = solver minus emulation mean, over the emulation's seed standard deviation) and relative difference <= 2.0%, across 1.1 (C=2), 2.1 (C=20) and 2.9 (C=200) decades of variance decay. Against analytic exp(-2 Omega t) while the ratio is above 0.36: within 0.71% in every run. Below that the solver and the emulation both decay more slowly than exp(-2 Omega t), +4.1% at a ratio of 0.08 (C=2, C=20) and +13% at 0.011 (C=200). Cause: IEM leaves cell means unchanged, and particles diffusing across faces carry the differences between neighbouring cell means - here the sampling noise of the random 0/1 start, variance 1/(4 N_pc) - into within-cell variance. With 256 particles per cell the solver's excess falls to +1.1% at a ratio of 0.078 and +4.0% at 0.010 (emulation: +1.0%, +3.75%), and the emulation gives +0.23% and +0.93% at 1024; in the emulation, frozen particles give no excess, and scattering the mean after the move instead of using the previous step's leaves it unchanged (+4.5% against +4.1%). So the departure is variance production by cell-mean differences, falling as 1/N_pc, not a kernel or ordering defect. Restart: the loaded state reproduces the step-100 within-cell variance exactly, and the continued run stays within 0.52% of the uninterrupted run through step 200, the Brownian paths differing because the random stream restarts.
result.threshold: Solver within 3 emulation standard deviations at every output step; analytic rate within 1% over the first e-fold of variance decay. Restart: continued decay within the uninterrupted run's statistical spread.

records.limitations: Zero flow, uniform Cartesian cells and constant Gamma; 2 ranks only. Verifies the implemented update and its coupling to the scatter, not the IEM model: no turbulent flow was run, so C_IEM = 2 and the LES mixing time scale V^(2/3)/(C_IEM Gamma_eff) are not validated against a measured scalar-variance decay. The emulation shares the solver's step order by construction; the fresh-mean variant shows that this ordering does not change the decay in this test, which has no mean flow. Up to 53% of particles left through the walls in the longest run; the pooled metric uses the survivors.

The discriminating quantities are the outer-layer u' (1.16 -> 1.06) and nu_t, which are reported but were not criteria; the corrected filter still carries 6% more outer u' and 20% less nu_t than the box filter. The corrected default was represented by width_ratio 1.5874 on the former build, equal to 1.6e-6 in alpha, not run on the corrected build. One grid, one Reynolds number.

records.question: On the HOM02 benchmark, how does the dynamic procedure with the simpson_ik test filter behave, and does weighting it as a two-direction filter correct it?

records.environment: Owner's Slurm cluster (TAMU Grace), PETSc 3.20.3 optimized, one node, 48 ranks (4 x 4 x 3). Runs les_dyn_homog_simpson_64_20261009-150850 (job 20075140) and les_dyn_homog_simpson_r1587_64_20261009-153918 (20075506), reduced with the matrix of hom02-les-execution-2026-10-09 by the HOM02 les_matrix.py.
records.configuration: As hom02-les-execution-2026-10-09 at 64^3: dynamic_smagorinsky, homogeneous averaging, clamp 0.3, cube_root_volume, test_filter simpson_ik; width_ratio 2.0 under the former alpha = 4, and width_ratio 1.5874 standing for the corrected alpha = 2^(4/3) (equal to 1.6e-6).

result.measured: Former weighting: whole-domain Cs 0.091 against the box filter's 0.194; nu_t/nu 1.36 against 3.69; cutoff-band mean log10 error +0.385 against +0.012 (no model +0.72); decay error up to 0.50 against 0.18; low-band RMS log10 0.184. Corrected weighting: Cs 0.168, nu_t/nu 3.05, cutoff band +0.116, decay error up to 0.26, low band 0.095. Both ran to the last DNS spectrum. tests/c/test_les.c dynamic-procedure-simpson-ratio-counts-filtered-directions fails on the former weighting and passes on the corrected one.
result.threshold: Characterization in the terms of hom02-les-execution-2026-10-09: runs to the last DNS spectrum and brings the cutoff band from the no-model +0.72 to within +-0.15.

records.limitations: Characterizes rather than validates: like every model in hom02-les-accuracy-2026-10-09, the corrected run does not keep decay within 10% of the DNS. A test filter that ignores one direction is a poor fit to isotropic turbulence; even corrected it leaves 10x the box filter's cutoff pile-up. Its intended use is planes homogeneous in i and k, which wmles-channel-retau1000-simpson-2026-10-09 covers.

records.question: Does the cabot wall function run the wall-modelled channel within the werner criteria?
records.commit: b85f5a07bb7bd8ed7241d1ce09ca75d98bbf1568 (pinned executables; job 20075145).
records.environment: Owner's Slurm cluster (TAMU Grace), PETSc 3.20.3 optimized, one node, 24 ranks (3 x 2 x 4), executables pinned at b85f5a0. Each variant restarted with --restart-from from step 100000 (t = 2000) of case_constant_flux_20261008-154731, the run behind wmles-channel-retau1000-werner-2026-10-09, with --statistics-state reset, and was cancelled at step 101154 (t = 2023.08) on the owner's instruction. Staged and reduced on the cluster by the case's wm_matrix/wm_matrix.py; its reducer reproduced the parent's published werner numbers to rounding before use. summary.csv and profiles.csv inspected as supplied.
records.configuration: examples/periodic_test/driven_channel/les_wallmodel_retau1000 at the parent's settings: 32 x 20 x 48 uniform cells over pi x 2 x 2 pi, constant_flux driven, Re_b = 40,000, Dual Time Picard Jameson RK, dt = 0.02, dynamic_smagorinsky with homogeneous averaging over i and k, clamp 0.3, cube_root_volume width. Statistics window t = 2200-2800 (halves split at 2500). Each variant changes one key from the parent: wall_function.model cabot. The pressure gradient enters from the resolved pressure at the first interior cell; the reference velocity is the second cell's (y = 0.15).

result.measured: From the first step after restart, on the state werner had just held at u_tau 0.0514: u_tau mean 0.0391, rms 0.0215 (3.4x the other models), minimum 0.003; mean over 1154 steps 0.0389. 46 momentum steps hit the attempt cap; 1.65 s/step against 0.32 for werner. Reproduced offline on the restart checkpoint by solving the implemented relation cell by cell: 0.03902 mean, 0.02147 rms; 36% of wall cells give a negative stress, which the solve folds positive. The same relation without its pressure-gradient term gives 0.0487 (-2.6%); with the driving force added to the gradient 0.0458; with the gradient smoothed over 5 x 5 cells 0.0427.
result.threshold: As the werner record; no window was reached, so only the friction-velocity criterion can be judged, and it fails by -22%.

records.limitations: Cancelled before its statistics window; the profile criteria were not evaluated. The cause is the formulation as implemented: the instantaneous resolved pressure gradient integrated across two cells is +-38% of the reference velocity, without the convective terms that balance it in the full boundary-layer equations, and the u_tau solve takes sqrt(|tau|). That diagnosis is offline on one state; a corrected cabot is unbuilt.

records.question: Does the rewritten pressure-Poisson solver, built once per run instead of every step, reproduce the previous solver and the existing pressure evidence, and what does keeping it save per step at production scale?
records.commit: 3709375 (0d34592 rewrite, 21e90ad separate pre/post smoothing counts); local equivalence checks at the working tree of 0d34592 against a 53ba654 binary
records.environment: Equivalence and duct: local WSL2 workstation, PETSc 3.20.3 debug build (-O0 -g3) with MPICH, 1 to 6 ranks. Speed and bend: TAMU Grace, PETSc 3.20.3 optimized (foss-2023a), Slurm; 96 ranks (4 x 4 x 6) for the LES pilot, 48 ranks (2 x 2 x 12) for the bend.
records.configuration: (a) Equivalence: the same staged run launched with the 53ba654 and the new simulator on flat_channel (25 x 25 x 97 cells, 1 and 4 ranks, 30 steps), bent_channel (4 ranks, 30 steps), the periodic driven laminar channel (4 ranks, 40 steps, then --continue at 2 ranks and --restart-from at 1 rank) and decaying isotropic turbulence 64^3 with Newton-Krylov momentum (4 ranks, 10 steps); checkpoints and Poisson convergence logs compared byte for byte. (b) The duct-poiseuille-picard-2026-09-18 configuration rerun on 3709375: n x n x 2n cells for n = 8, 16, 24 on 2, 4, 6 ranks, uniform programmatic grid in place of the original grid_gen box. (c) The Re_b 4410 square-duct wall-resolved LES pilot les_pilot_r96_dt002_lv, 0.52M cells, 3 multigrid levels, dt 0.02, 200 steps, statistics off, PETSc log_view, compared with the same pilot on 53ba654 (2026-10-09). (d) The Humphrey Re = 790 laminar bend, 48 x 48 x 384, Newton-Krylov point-block, 4 levels, 4500 steps, rerun from the 2026-10-07 configuration.

result.measured: (a) Bitwise identical checkpoints and byte-identical Poisson convergence logs in every case, including the continuation marker; -malloc_dump reported no leaks. (b) Velocity relative L2 error 3.49e-2, 9.67e-3, 4.39e-3 (order 1.85, 1.95) and axial pressure-gradient error 5.89e-2, 1.54e-2, 6.92e-3 (order 1.93, 1.98), identical to the 2026-09-18 record to the printed digits; maximum divergence at most 5.5e-8. (c) 4.454 to 1.482 s per step (3.0x); the Poisson solve 3.444 to 0.492 s per step (7.0x); PCSetUp 1800 to 606 calls and MatLUFactorNum 600 to 3 over 200 steps, with identical PCApply (9960) and MatSolve (36531) counts. At step 200 the velocity agreed with the old build to 1.1e-12 relative and the pressure by a constant 1.08e-7 offset over the interior (a gauge shift); the optimized cluster builds are not bitwise identical. (d) 4500 of 4500 steps converged and committed with the same convergence-reason counts as humphrey-laminar-bend-nk-pointblock-2026-10-07, maximum divergence 3.37e-10, 47:49 against 1:11:49; station-plane velocity within 6.9e-9 of the 2026-10-07 run and pressure by a constant 1.36e-6, so the RMS residuals against HTW 1977 Fig. 2 stay 0.073, 0.185, 0.184, 0.138 to the three printed decimals (bounded by the velocity difference, not recomputed from the new extracts).
result.threshold: Equivalence to the previous solver at round-off (bitwise where the build is unoptimized); the duct and bend evidence reproduced; a reduction in Poisson cost per step on the LES pilot.

records.limitations: No new physics is validated: (b) and (d) re-establish existing evidence for the rewritten code, and the bend residual against experiment remains about twice the measurement floor as recorded on 2026-10-07. The bitwise check covers single-block cases on a debug build; on the optimized cluster build the solvers agree to round-off and a pressure gauge, which was measured but not explained. The 3.0x speed-up is for one 96-rank LES configuration; the 4.2M-cell DNS duct was not measured. Static geometry only: immersed or moving bodies, which would change the operator during a run, remain refused.
